strategy.summary: Reproduce the non-metric SMACOF bug in sklearn.manifold._mds (PR 30514, fixing issues 16846, 18933, 26999, 27028): on the buggy revision the stress increases across iterations, the returned stress does not match the returned embedding, and IsotonicRegression/smacof fail on the issue 26999 dissimilarity matrix; on the fixed revision these tests pass. Build the buggy commit 692289e4939d from source with a compiler toolchain (sklearn is Cython), install numpy/scipy compatible with that revision, then run the four added tests in sklearn/manifold/tests/test_mds.py.

system_packages: gcc or clang with C/C++ toolchain
libopenblas or default BLAS via build system
build_commands: pip install -r build_requirements or pip install cython meson-python ninja numpy scipy joblib threadpoolctl pytest
pinned_because: numpy 1.22.0 minimum is documented in README NumPyMinVersion and the reporter used 1.25.1; respected as documented constraint
scipy 1.8.0 minimum is documented in README SciPyMinVersion and the reporter used 1.11.1; respected as documented constraint

Python 3.10 is the repository minimum per the PR/README, while the traceback path indicates 3.9.5; the 3.9.5 version is from the issue and is era-inferred, so prefer the repository-supported minimum 3.10 if the build fails on 3.9
scikit-learn itself is unbounded: no documented constraint and no era table entry, so the buggy checkout itself is used rather than any released version

strategy.reproducing_test: sklearn/manifold/tests/test_mds.py::test_nonmetric_mds_optimization, test_isotonic_outofbounds, test_returned_stress, test_nonmetric_lower_normalized_stress (added by the PR diff)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 692289e4939d, at least one of the added tests fails: test_nonmetric_mds_optimization fails because stress after 2 iterations is not greater than stress after 3 iterations (the stress increases), test_isotonic_outofbounds raises out-of-bounds or NaN ValueError, and test_returned_stress fails because the returned stress does not match the embedding. On the fixed revision (PR 30514 applied) all these tests pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: Run MDS(n_components=2, n_init=1, eps=1e-15, max_iter=2/3, metric=False, random_state=42) on the 200-row digits subset and compare stress_ values; the buggy code yields stress_after_2_iter <= stress_after_3_iter.

input_output_examples.input: it: 0, stress 3355940054.205797; it: 1, stress 33534.27419788723; it: 2, stress 33605.33211344484 (non-metric MDS, verbose=2, init=Z1)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: breaking at iteration 2 with stress 33605.33211344484 (loss increases after iteration 1 and algorithm stops)
input_output_examples.expected_output: stress should decrease monotonically across iterations rather than increase from 33534.27419788723 to 33605.33211344484

risks: Build requires a C/C++ toolchain and Cython; a failed build or mismatched numpy ABI will prevent any transition.

The defect is numerical and depends on BLAS/OpenMP threading; the reporter used OpenBLAS with libgomp, and results may differ under other BLAS backends or thread counts, so pin OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and record the backend.
Python version is uncertain: 3.9.5 is from the issue traceback while the repository requires 3.10; a version mismatch could prevent building the buggy revision.

The issue 26999 NaN/out-of-bounds behaviour is triggered by machine-precision dissimilarities (6.66e-16); platform floating-point differences (e.g. aarch64 vs x86_64) could change whether isotonic regression raises at all, so the test may not fail on non-x86 platforms.
test_nonmetric_mds_optimization depends on load_digits data and random_state=42 subsampling; it is sensitive to the numpy version's RNG behaviour and the sklearn data files.
test_returned_stress and test_mds_recovers_true_data use default n_init and random_state; if the buggy code's random path differs, the failure may not be deterministic across machines.

No sanitiser or architecture-specific behaviour is evidenced; if the bug only appears under a particular platform, the test will not transition elsewhere and that should be reported rather than assumed.
scikit-learn version is unbounded in the evidence; the buggy commit is used directly, so no released-version pin is applied.

oracle.tolerance: assert_allclose default rtol for returned-stress test (rtol=1e-7) and atol=1e-10 for recovers-true-data test
oracle.reference_source: euclidean_distances computed stress in test_returned_stress; stress-1 formula from doc/modules/manifold.rst
oracle.why: Stress comparisons are continuous-valued, so the oracle is a tolerance check on the stress reported by the estimator against stress recomputed from the returned embedding; the monotonicity check is an ordering comparison.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: test_nonmetric_mds_optimization asserts stress after 2 iterations > stress after 3 iterations; on the buggy revision the stress increases across iterations (e.g. 33534.27 to 33605.33), so the assertion is False and the test fails. test_isotonic_outofbounds raises ValueError (out-of-bounds or Input contains NaN) because the isotonic regression runs before the first SMACOF update and fails on the near-zero dissimilarity. test_returned_stress fails because the returned stress is from the previous iteration and does not equal the stress recomputed from the returned embedding.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With PR 30514 applied, SMACOF updates before isotonic regression, the stress is computed after the update, the disparities are symmetric, and IsotonicRegression uses out_of_bounds="clip"; all four added tests pass.
